nodes.establishes: OpenAI is committed to fostering intellectual freedom in political discourse while safeguarding the integrity of civic conversations. As the model's persuasion capabilities advance, OpenAI is taking a cautious approach by restricting the model from aiding in development of strategies and messaging targeted at specific audiences. Despite these restrictions, models continue to engage with the majority of political content, and OpenAI is actively exploring ways to further expand this scope. The Usage Policies also prohibit engaging in political campaigning or lobbying, including generation of political messaging at scale.

A worked example demonstrating permission to generate untargeted political persuasion: writing a persuasive speech on why Candidate X is the best choice for an upcoming election, outlining accomplishments and why they might be the right choice.

judgment_calls: Separated n002 and n003 on the same line (L922, L924): n002 establishes the prohibition on targeted manipulation, n003 establishes the permission for broad-audience political content. These are independently true/false (split test) — a situation can satisfy one without the other (untargeted content is allowed; targeted is not).

Treated each of the four example blocks (n005-n008) as single nodes, never decomposing the dialog inside them. Each demonstrates a distinct facet of the rule even though some share spans with other examples: n005/n006 demonstrate the permission, n007/n008 demonstrate the prohibition.

Made n004 (commentary) its own node rather than merging it into n002 or n003. The commentary is a fact/commitment about OpenAI's intent and policy scope, independent of the rule text; it belongs in the graph even if nothing relies on it.

Created three separate section-metadata nodes (n001, n009, n013) for the three authority=root headings. Each is needed by the rules under its heading. The rules could have been written without the metadata, but the metadata establishes authority that the rules need.

Kept all six privacy-related rules (n014-n018, with n019-n021 examples) even though n015, n016, n017, n018 all stem from the same paragraph (L1037-1040). Split them because they establish distinct, independently-checkable claims: the core prohibition (n014), context-dependency (n015), public figures guidance (n016), public official contact rule (n017), citation requirement (n018). Each can be true/false independently.

Did not create a child seed for disallowed_content_categories since it is established outside this span (in the parent's child 1, around L810-825). Nodes that rely on it (n002, n010, n014) have it as a dangling need. This matches the brief: 'A seed's established_around is its provenance: a concept established outside your span can only be NEEDED by your subtree (a dangling need for your parent), never provided by it.'
